result.movement: It moved one point, and only because three of the six shipped items are genuinely live to real users: the 30-day back-catalogue (verified rendering 30 replay rows on prod), streak repair (server RPC live, `repair_login_streak` string present in the live bundle), and streak-aware reminder copy (confirmed in prod `pg_proc`). What did NOT move is the thing that was wrong last time: reach. Web push went 0 → 1 subscriber in ~36 hours live, and subscriber #1 is Alex (docs/PRE-SEASON-CHECKLIST.md line 9 says so; the row's endpoint is a desktop Chrome/FCM endpoint created 2026-08-20 11:12 with tz_offset +120). The Android widget and the Android FCM rail — the two headline commits — reach exactly ZERO users, because both live in versionCode 20 and Play still serves vc19 (docs/TODO.md:5). `device_tokens` has 0 android rows. And the outcome numbers are flat: 30 live-streak accounts today vs 32 on 2026-08-19; 19 holding streak>=2 vs 17; DAU 26, WAU 44. The panel was right the first time and the fix is still one Play upload and one Xcode session away from being real.
result.verdict: The streak machine is now better than most competitors' — forgiving tick rules, auto-shields, a real 30-day archive that cannot be farmed, and a server-authoritative same-day repair — and for the people already inside it, it works: 29.3% D1, DAU/WAU 0.59. But it reaches almost nobody. 36 of 205 profiles have any push channel (35 iOS, 1 web, 0 Android), the widget is in an unpublished build, and Clarity shows 3 returning users against 190 new ones on /play over 8 days. Excellent mechanics, no distribution.
strengths: The 14-day gate the last panel flagged as 'one gate away' was closed properly, not cosmetically. Archive saves in Footle/Trail/Mystery carry an `arc` stamp, all three streak walks break on it, and form14 dims arc-only days as 'caught up later' (src/screens/DailyScreen.jsx:629-648). I loaded prod as a signed-in account and counted the result: 30 rows of Recent Days back to Jul 23, each unplayed cell an ↺ replay control, Daily 7 deliberately left yesterday-only. Back-filling cannot repaint the form or extend the streak. That is a better archive than Wordle's (paywalled) and honest in a way most streak UIs are not.

Streak repair is engineered, not bolted on. `tick_login_streak` stashes {fell, fellDay} on an un-shielded break, `repair_login_streak(int)` is single-use, same-local-day, authenticated-only, and ends with explicit REVOKEs from public and anon (supabase/migrations/v1_6_streak_repair.sql:166-186). The client dispatches `biq:archive-completed` from all four modes and the shell repairs only when the completed day is yesterday. Both the RPC and the client string are live in the production bundle (/assets/index-Bnf4vgjN.js).

The web daily reminder now writes streak-aware copy at send time — the exact quick win the last panel asked for, verified in prod `pg_proc.prosrc`: '🔥 {n}-day streak — one puzzle tonight makes it {n+1}' for live streaks, 'Your best run is {n} days — tonight is a good night to start the climb' for lapsed ones. The hourly cron has succeeded on every run (cron.job_run_details jobid=2, 8 consecutive 'succeeded' through 2026-08-21 12:00 UTC).

For the players who get inside the loop, the loop holds. Cohort of 75 users who first recorded a score 9-60 days ago: 29.3% returned on D1, 49.3% returned somewhere in D2-D8. DAU 26 against WAU 44 is a 0.59 stickiness ratio — Duolingo-class for the surviving core. The problem is not that the habit fails; it is that almost nobody is offered it.

The SEO club pages carry their own account-free return streak — a global (not per-club) day-index streak in localStorage with a 'come back tomorrow' ribbon, written directly into the generated HTML (scripts/gen-seo-pages.mjs, `BQ_SKEY='biq.quiz.streak'`, `bumpStreak()`). Its own source comment names the reason: 95% of sessions view exactly one page. This is the single smartest retention decision in the repo and it sits on the surface that carries ~47% of impressions.

The Android widget's state model is right even though nobody has it: one-way data (app pushes {date,done,total,streak} through WidgetBridgePlugin → SharedPreferences), the provider only judges staleness, and a yesterday-stamped snapshot renders 'New puzzles ready' — the lapsed-user hook — with hourly updatePeriodMillis existing solely to cross midnight (android/app/src/main/java/app/balliq/DailyWidgetProvider.java:29-80).
weaknesses: The two flagship commits reach zero users. `device_tokens` contains 35 iOS rows and 0 Android rows. The Android widget (1c4d615) and the FCM rail (60d14ed) both landed in versionCode 20; Play still serves vc19 (docs/TODO.md:5). FCM was proved with a deliberately fake token — a transport-level handshake test, not a delivery to a person. Until vc20 is published, Android remote push and the widget are, in retention terms, unwritten code.

The web-push ask shipped and produced one subscriber, who is the developer. `web_push_subscriptions` = 1 row, created 2026-08-20 11:12 UTC, endpoint fcm.googleapis.com (desktop Chrome), tz_offset_minutes = 120; docs/PRE-SEASON-CHECKLIST.md line 9 states plainly 'Alex = subscriber #1'. The reason is structural, not conversion: src/App.jsx:9561 hard-returns on `!user?.id`, so the ask never fires for a guest — and guests are the overwhelming majority of the web surface the ask was built to reach.

Measured web retention is 1.6%. Microsoft Clarity, pages containing /play, 2026-08-14 → 2026-08-21: 190 distinct new users, 3 distinct returning users (7 sessions). Site-wide over the last 3 days: 325 new users, 8 returning, 1.17 pages per session. No amount of streak design has touched this number.

57% of the signed-in base never came back a second day. Of 179 accounts holding streak state, 102 have best = 1 — they lit the flame once and never returned. Only 54 ever reached best>=3, which is also the minimum streak length that qualifies for repair (src/App.jsx:8465, `prevStreak >= 3`), so the repair feature is structurally unavailable to two-thirds of the base.

Streak repair cannot bring anyone back — it can only reward someone who already came back. The window is the same local day the break is discovered (`v_fell_day <> v_today` refuses, v1_6_streak_repair.sql:166-168), the only surface that announces it is a 💔 banner on the Daily screen, and nothing pushes or emails the news that a streak broke. Right now `login_streak ? 'fell'` matches 0 rows in prod — nobody has ever stood in the doorway. Duolingo's version works because the notification is the feature.

The archive has no depth for the people who most need a reason to stay. `firstTime` initialises to today and only widens from the user's own local history (src/screens/DailyScreen.jsx:517-539), so a first-time or guest player sees exactly ONE row in Recent Days. I confirmed it on the booted iPhone 17 simulator: '0 day streak — play one puzzle to light it', a blank 14-cell form strip, and a Recent Days table containing only 'Today · Aug 21'. Roughly 30 days × 3 modes of ready content is invisible to the ~190 new /play users of the last 8 days.

Two of the four daily modes lose their history on any device change. useAuth.jsx back-syncs and rehydrates `daily_scores` and `wordle_state` only (lines 485-570); Trail and Mystery history exist solely as localStorage keys with no remote column, so switching browser, clearing site data, or moving web→app silently erases half the form record and shortens the archive.

Still no email channel anywhere in the repo, and still no iOS widget — and iOS is where all 35 push tokens and the approved 1.6.0 build live. The one platform with a real installed base has the fewest zero-permission return triggers.

The opt-in sheet does not use the asset it is selling. src/App.jsx:11367-11370 reads 'Keep your streak alive · Get one friendly reminder each evening…' — generic, at a moment when the player's actual streak number is already in scope and is the highest-converting thing you could put in that sentence.

The club-page return streak — the best-placed mechanic in the product — is unmeasured. It fires `bqev('clubq-play')`, `clubq-finish` and tags `clubq-streak`, but bqev is a bare `window.clarity('event', n)` call (scripts/gen-seo-pages.mjs:1107) and Clarity's smart-event breakdown for the last 7 days returns nothing for those names. Nobody knows whether the one hook sitting on 47% of impressions works.

five_star_moves.title: Turn the streak break into an outbound event
five_star_moves.why: Repair today is same-local-day, streak>=3, and discoverable only by opening the app — so it can reward a returner but never create one. Send the break ('your 8-day streak broke — one puzzle before midnight brings it back') over whichever channel the user has, widen the window to 48h, and drop the >=3 floor to >=2 so it covers the 102 users stuck at best=1. That is Duolingo's actual mechanic; Ball IQ has built the half that doesn't reach out.

five_star_moves.title: Build the email channel
five_star_moves.why: Still absent from src/ and supabase/functions entirely. 205 profiles carry an address. It is the only channel that needs no permission prompt, survives an uninstall and a cleared localStorage, and reaches the 169 of 205 accounts with no push token at all. A weekly 'your form last week + the archive you missed' digest is the cheapest way to address the 57% who never came back a second day.

result.area: Social & viral loops (invites, challenge links, share cards, multiplayer, friends)
result.movement: It did not move — and on the evidence now available it should come down one notch. What shipped since 2026-08-19 is MEASUREMENT, not loops: scripts/k-factor.sql (7ae5476) and the challenge_events table + RPC (58c14b7), plus a winner haptic on MP Game Over (1f272d5). That was the last panel's quick-win #1 and it was executed well. But every loop mechanism in production is byte-identical to 08-19, and the measurement it bought reports worse news than the last panel guessed: re-running k-factor today gives 10 invite signups / 43 active = k(7d) 0.23, statistically identical to 08-20's 9/40; friendships formed in 30d is still 0; challenge_events has ZERO rows in ~24h of live instrumentation (verified the RPC call is in the live bundle, so that zero is real, not a broken detector). The last panel's quick-win #3 (guest entry at /join) was fully BUILT on 2026-08-20 — and it is sitting on branch claude/suspicious-yonath-1e30b0, not on main, not deployed, needing two Alex steps. Effort went in; production state is unchanged. Grading effort would be the failure mode this panel exists to avoid.
result.verdict: The loop machinery is genuinely above category — five endpoints, real server-rendered OG cards, deterministic head-to-head, Universal Links, in-app-webview escapes — and it converts approximately nothing: k stuck at 0.23, zero friendships in 30 days, zero challenge-link opens since instrumentation went live, and 10 of 10 invite-driven signups have never recorded a single game. The two loops that could actually move it are structurally blocked: multiplayer walls BOTH sender and recipient behind sign-up (while the share card promises "free, no sign-up"), and Footle — the #1 mode at 307 plays/30d — ships a bare link with no token, no personalised card and no return channel.
strengths: The recipient-side engineering is real and better than the competitive field. /c/5.20260821.Marius returns a correct personalised card (og:title "Marius scored 5/7 on the Daily 7 ⚽") and hands the token forward as /play?c=5.20260821.Marius rather than dropping it — I curl'd it and watched the redirect preserve the payload. api/join.js:29-40 documents three different room-code alphabets and deliberately mirrors the looser client one so a valid code can never lose its card. api/c.js:74-80 re-canonicalises %2E so a dotted name survives the app's dot-splitting parser. This is careful work.

The /c/ challenge loop is now genuinely measurable, which it was not on 08-19. challenge_events + record_challenge_event() are applied to prod, and I confirmed record_challenge_event appears in the live bundle at /assets/GameRoot-DahLjEn-.js — so the read is trustworthy in both directions. The last panel said "nobody knows the k-factor"; now somebody can.

Footle's end screen gives share the PRIMARY filled button, not the ghost secondary the last panel described app-wide — I solved TORRES in 2 on the simulator and "Share result" is the green button, with "Bad answer? Tell us" and the Daily 7 cross-sell below it. The tap economy on the sender side is fine; the problem is downstream of the tap.

The invite loop still out-converts everything else the app has: 126 rooms in 7 days, 83 of them (66%) received a guest, producing 10 of 36 signups (28%). No other channel in the product has that hit rate — it is worth fixing precisely because it is the only one that works at all.
Home puts "Play with Friends — Invite friends / Same phone" above the fold as a full-width card, so the social path is not buried; the discoverability half of the problem is solved.

result.area: Content quality of the question bank (the moat)
result.movement: Half the previous panel's quick wins landed on 2026-08-20 and one of them was the valuable half: hard questions with no explanation went 155 → 4, and the 2026 World Cup future-tense stems were flipped. That is real and it moved the explanation axis up. But it did not move the grade up, and I am moving it down slightly for two reasons the last panel did not test. First, the freshness gap it flagged is unchanged and the calendar has advanced past it: the "season-freshness wave" commit (d9f8821) changed exactly ONE line of src/questions.js and the bank still contains zero summer-2026 transfers, zero 2026-27 content, and zero mentions of Iraola — while balliq.app's own Liverpool FAQ knows Slot left and Iraola arrived 4 June 2026. Second, I checked the QA process behind the accuracy and found it switched off: question_review's newest row is 2026-06-09, and 0 of 20 sampled questions from the August EFL wave have a review record. In the fresh, unreviewed content I found a keyed answer that is now factually wrong and two wrong hints — including one written on 2026-08-20 in the very commit that closed the hints backlog. The previous 8 was defensible for what it measured; it measured the artefact and not the process that maintains it.
result.verdict: The bank is still far deeper than anything it competes with — 6,694 questions, 84% explained, zero structural defects, and difficulty labels that real player data validates almost perfectly — but the machinery that made it accurate has been off since 9 June while ~600 questions shipped, and the bank enters the 2026-27 season with nothing a fan has argued about in the last twelve months. Depth is holding; freshness and quality control are both slipping.
strengths: Difficulty labels are validated by real players, not by taste: 7 days of club_quiz_results (205 plays, 2,036 answered items) give easy 89.7% correct, medium 69.2%, hard 50.3%, overall 68.6%. That is a textbook ladder — the 'hard' tier is a genuine coin-flip and 'easy' is a genuine gimme. No competitor app publishes anything like this and most do not have the tiers at all.

The highest-value explanation gap is closed. Hard questions with no explanation went 155 → 4 in one commit (820eb4b, 151 hints); overall coverage 5,475 → 5,626 (81.8% → 84.0%). The losing player — the one who most needs a reason to come back — now almost always gets the story.

Explanation quality is narrative, not restatement, and it holds on the public surface: the live Liverpool page serves 'A groundsman pitched the friendlier Welcome to Anfield — Shankly changed it to the curt, menacing This Is Anfield' and 'Bruce Grobbelaar's spaghetti legs antics helped Liverpool win the shootout in Roma's own stadium'. Rival apps ship an answer key.

Depth against the actual competitive set is not close. The top Play Store / App Store football quiz apps advertise 'over 1000 questions' with no explanations (Bold Cat Football Quiz - Soccer Trivia; Football Quiz! Ultimate Trivia). Ball IQ is 6.7× that with an explanation on 5 of every 6.

Structural hygiene remains perfect and gated: 0 duplicate options, 0 invalid answer indices, 0 stray whitespace, 0 exact duplicate stems across 6,687 MCQs; audit-open-claims passes clean on all 6,694 and audit-distractor-plausibility passes with 'no near-name/anachronism pairs · PL era clean'.

Accuracy on new content is still high in absolute terms: 23 of 24 sampled questions from the six newest (unreviewed) EFL club packs are correct, including non-obvious details — Portsmouth's 2008 FA Cup as their first major trophy in ~58 years, Wrexham bottom of the whole Football League the season before beating champions Arsenal, Norwich as the first English club to win at Bayern's Olympiastadion.
weaknesses: THE REVIEW PROCESS IS DORMANT AND UNREVIEWED CONTENT IS SHIPPING WITH ERRORS. question_review holds 4,102 rows, all last touched 2026-06-09, and it rejected 12.5% of what it saw (513 of 4,102). Since then the Portuguese wave, the 8-club EFL wave and the freshness wave all shipped: 0 of 20 sampled Wrexham/Derby/Stoke ids appear in the table at all. That rejection rate applied to ~600 unreviewed questions implies roughly 75 that would not have passed.

A KEYED ANSWER IS NOW WRONG. q_0f2027 'Atletico Madrid's stadium capacity is approximately how many?' keys 68,000. The Metropolitano has held 70,460 since September 2023 and 70,692 today — and '72,000' is one of the four options, so the bank marks the closest answer wrong. audit-open-claims does not catch it: needsAnchor() on that stem returns false, so the whole 'X is approximately' present-state class (q_d6f747 Allianz is the other) sits outside the gate.

Two wrong hints in content written after the last panel. src/questions.js:6654 says Banks 'made the famous save from Pelé two years before joining the Stoke side that won at Wembley' — he joined Stoke in April 1967, three years BEFORE the 1970 save. q_837628's hint says 'Mexico have reached 17 World Cups' when the same bank treats the 2026 tournament as played in 42 other stems, making it 18. The bank is a full season behind its own marketing pages. Zero questions mention Iraola, the summer-2026 window, or 2026-27; the newest transfer fact is Wirtz in June 2025. The live Liverpool FAQ, by contrast, answers 'Who is Liverpool's manager now?' with 'Andoni Iraola, appointed on 4 June 2026 after Arne Slot departed at the end of a trophyless 2025-26 season.' The freshest football knowledge in the product is on the page nobody plays.

Breadth is diluting depth. 17 of 86 club packs now hold under 30 questions and 12 hold 20 or fewer — the eight EFL-wave clubs are all 15-16 (Wrexham 16, Derby 16, Stoke 16, Sheffield Wednesday 15, Hajduk Split 15). result.verdict: Footle is genuinely good — the keyboard fix landed, the grading is correct, and the win screen beats Wordle's on onward routing. Everything around it is uneven: the most-repeated moment in the product (a correct MCQ answer) still just changes colour, the whole sound layer ships off, the newest mode is the plainest screen in the app, and the celebration work of the last 48 hours went to the mode with six lifetime plays.
strengths: Footle's keyboard fix (a71cade) is real and verified by hand: 12 consecutive key taps across three rows — including the leftmost 'A' at x=21pt, which sits at the screen edge — all registered first-time with zero misfires. The Wordle grading is also correct on the hard case: guessing SANTOS against TORRES marked the first S absent and the final S green (duplicate-letter handling), with the keyboard graded to match.

The Footle win screen is the best celebration in the product and, on one axis, better than Wordle's: confetti, '⚽ Brilliant!', the answer named in full ('Fernando Torres'), +54 XP, Share, a 'Bad answer? Tell us' escape hatch, a NEXT countdown (09:07:12), AND an onward CTA — 'Not done yet? Play today's Daily 7 →'. Wordle's modal just shows stats and stops.

Every Daily 7 question carries a '💡 Why?' explanation on the reveal — I hit 4 of 4 and all four were specific and well-written (the Capello/Cruyff 1994 one names all four scorers). No mainstream football quiz competitor does this per-question. It is the strongest single reason the quiz engine holds attention (Clarity: 103.4s average active time on /play, 92.6% scroll depth over 7 days).

Stadiums' typed-answer recognition has the right Sporcle feel: 'anfield' and 'emirates' both committed on keystroke without pressing Enter, the counter ticked 0→1→2 instantly, and solved rows land newest-first in a stable alphabetical board. Progress persisted correctly across leaving and re-entering the mode (2/20 preserved).

The Daily hub is the strongest information design in the app: 'NEW PUZZLES IN 9h 11m', per-mode colour coding, live state on the card ('✓ Solved in 2'), '1 of 4 played', a two-week streak strip, and a Recent Days matrix showing each mode's result per day. Footle's guess-count and streak both surface there correctly after a solve.

Alex acts on review findings fast and completely — all five gaps the previous panel named were closed within 24 hours, each with a code comment citing the panel and the reason for the specific implementation choice (e.g. why the streak pill is position:fixed rather than mounted into the header).
weaknesses: The correct-answer reveal — the single most-repeated moment in the entire product — has NO motion. `.opt.correct` (app.css:585) sets background, border-color and color and nothing else; there is no keyframe, no scale, no transform on the correct state. I watched it four times in Daily 7: the card just tints a faint rgba(88,204,2,0.12) green. Duolingo bounces its answer bar, Kahoot flashes full-screen. This was the previous panel's five-star move and it did not land.

The new mobile streak beat misfires on iPhone. On the question where the 3-in-a-row pill should fire, the pill was not visible in either of two screenshots taken over ~4 seconds — instead a stray 'Next →' painted in the status-bar strip, overlapping the Dynamic Island, and persisted across both screenshots before clearing on the next question. No other reveal in the run produced it. `.streak-beat` is position:fixed/z-index:60 and `.next-btn-primary` is position:sticky/bottom:16px/z-index:5 — the flagship new feedback beat is currently invisible-plus-artifact on the device it was built for.

Stadiums — the newest mode, shipped and expanded to five leagues in the last 48 hours — is the plainest surface in the app. The league picker is five identical flat grey rows with no crests, no league colour, no imagery, and ~45% of the screen left black. Compare the Club Quizzes picker in the SAME app: club colour gradients, crest tiles, league grouping, search across 76 clubs. Same product, wildly different care, and the undesigned one is the one that just shipped.

A wrong answer in Stadiums leaves the player with nothing useful. The text is NOT cleared (StadiumGame.jsx:161-163 fires haptic + shake only), so you must manually delete it before the next attempt in a mode built for rapid-fire typing. And the 'shake' is a single `transform: translateX(-4px)` toggled on for 420ms with a 0.12s transition (StadiumGame.jsx:223) — it leans 4px, sits there for a third of a second, then slides back. That is not a shake.

Stadiums has zero telemetry in practice: `scores` has ZERO rows for game_mode='stadiums' all-time, and the handler only writes on full completion or explicit give-up (App.jsx:9809-9826). A player who names 12 of 20 and closes the app is completely invisible — which is exactly the partial-completion signal a completion-run mode lives or dies on, and exactly the mistake the code comment says was learned from Mystery.

Effort is going where the players aren't. 30-day plays: footle 307/62 players, daily 272/55, survival 168/29, classic 120/38, trail 74/26 — but mystery is 6 plays from 4 players (all-time, since 2026-08-15). The whole celebration commit's headline item was Mystery's confetti. Footle and Daily 7 together are 78% of measured play and received no feel work in that window.

Mystery's warmth signal is still knowingly wrong and now has confetti on top of it. mysteryPlayer.js:148 still awards 150 of the 1000-point similarity max for `p.nat === answer.nat`, on a field the file's own header (MysteryPlayer.jsx:18-45) measures as wrong for Messi, Vinícius and James (all read 'Spain'), with nat===country for 5,277 of 8,489 pool entries. 15% of the steering signal is noise in a game whose entire mechanic is trusting the rank.

The whole audio layer is still dark: `sound: false` in the settings defaults (App.jsx:8238). Every chime, the streak arpeggio and the daily_complete chord that the juice commit just extended to three more modes play to almost nobody. Duolingo ships sound on.

The 'More modes' grid is ten monochrome grey cards with identical outline icons, no best score, no last-played, no state of any kind — for an app with 13-17 DAU. Nothing on that screen tells a player which of ten modes to pick, and the SQL says chaos (26), hotstreak (25), legends (23), league:LaLiga (2), league:Ligue1 (1) are rounding errors.

Phone ergonomics on the quiz: on Daily 7 all four options finish at ~64% of screen height and the bottom third of a 6.3" display is empty black until the answer lands. The thumb zone is unused. Footle after the first guess leaves ~150pt of dead black below the ENTER bar while the board above is cramped.

Footle's win panel omits the two numbers a daily player wants at the moment of victory: the solve count ('2/6') and the Footle streak. Both exist — but only on the Home card, after you back out of the game. Wordle puts both in the modal you cannot miss.

result.verdict: The engineering is genuinely good — the native no-analytics guard is real and Sentry's PII scrubbing is above the bar for a solo dev — but the compliance artefacts have drifted badly from the code: Microsoft Clarity session-replays ~87%-EEA/UK traffic with zero consent mechanism, the in-app privacy policy never mentions Clarity at all, the policy promises an EEA consent prompt that provably does not exist, and Play's live Data Safety form omits the crash-log collection Sentry actually does. This is worse than anyone realised — not because of what the app collects, but because every document describing it is wrong.
strengths: The native guard is real and I verified it end-to-end. Clarity and AdSense are injected only when !isNative (index.html:221-296), Vercel Web Analytics is gated at src/main.jsx:258, SpeedInsights at src/App.jsx:12154, Sentry performance tracing at src/main.jsx:51 (tracesSampleRate: isNative ? 0 : 0.1). The Capacitor app genuinely runs no third-party analytics — the store claim holds.

Sentry PII scrubbing is better than most funded teams ship. beforeSend deletes user.email and user.username, strips the URL fragment (where Supabase returns access_token after OAuth/magic-link), redacts access_token/refresh_token/provider_token/code/token/apikey from request.url AND from breadcrumb url/to/from, and deletes Authorization + apikey breadcrumb headers (src/main.jsx:40-74).

Apple's live App Privacy label is an accurate description of the native app: Data Linked to You = Contact Info, User Content, Identifiers, Usage Data; Data Not Linked = Diagnostics; no 'Data Used to Track You'. That matches the code.

All 17 prod tables have RLS enabled (list_tables on blcisypmngimqkwxrrdm: profiles, scores, friendships, question_review, user_game_state, game_rooms, room_players, user_reports, user_blocks, question_reports, notifications, device_tokens, room_answer_keys, room_answers, club_quiz_results, web_push_subscriptions, challenge_events — rls_enabled true on every one).

In-app account deletion is real and visible: Settings > DATA > Delete account, seen on the simulator running v1.6.2, and Play's public listing carries the 'You can request that data be deleted' practice.

Ads + the Funding Choices CMP were switched off rather than left loading dormant (index.html:245, src/lib/ads.js:18) — that removed two third-party scripts, the _GRECAPTCHA/NID cookies and a banner obligation from the web surface. Good call, correctly reasoned in the comment.
weaknesses: RECTIFY-CLASS, LIVE NOW: Microsoft Clarity session-records EU/UK traffic with no consent mechanism of any kind. On a single load of https://balliq.app/play I measured 5 POSTs to https://k.clarity.ms/collect and 0 DOM elements matching /consent|cookie|gdpr/. Clarity reports 2,224 sessions / 2,133 distinct users in the last 30d; the top-10 countries are 87% UK+EEA (UK 297, Norway 110, Italy 29, Spain 23, Netherlands 19, Denmark 16 of 567 in 7d). Controller established in Norway → GDPR Art 6 + ekomloven §2-7b + UK PECR all bite, and session replay is the textbook example regulators name as requiring prior consent. Unmitigated, and it has been live for the entire measurement window.

The privacy policy shown AT THE POINT OF COLLECTION does not mention Clarity. The React PrivacyScreen (src/App.jsx:6745) — what a balliq.app/play user reads while Clarity is recording them — omits Microsoft Clarity entirely; grep for 'Clarity' in that JSX block returns 0. Only the static public/privacy.html:81,90 names it. I confirmed this visually on the device: the in-app 'short version' reads '...cookieless analytics — but the app itself...' where the web version reads '...cookieless analytics and Microsoft Clarity session analytics...'. The file's own header (public/privacy.html:2-10) says this drift was caught in Sprint #83 and re-synced in #84. It has re-drifted, and the comment did not stop it.

The policy asserts a consent prompt that provably does not exist. public/privacy.html:82 and src/App.jsx:6777: 'If you are in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, you will be asked for your consent choices through a Google-certified consent prompt before any personalised ads are shown.' Ads and the CMP were switched off 2026-08-12 (index.html:245 ADS_ACTIVE = false; src/lib/ads.js:18 AD_CLIENT = ''). A regulator who reads that sentence, loads the site, finds no prompt, and then sees k.clarity.ms/collect firing, has a complaint that writes itself. This is the single most damaging sentence in the document.

Play's live Data Safety form under-declares. play.google.com/store/apps/datasafety?id=app.balliq lists exactly: Device or other IDs; App activity → App interactions; Photos and videos → Photos; Personal info → Email address and User IDs. There is no 'App info and performance → Crash logs / Diagnostics' — yet src/main.jsx:30 initialises Sentry unconditionally whenever VITE_SENTRY_DSN is set, and only tracing is native-gated (line 51); error events ship from the Android app. Apple's label DOES declare Diagnostics. The two stores contradict each other and Play is the wrong one. Data Safety under-declaration is an enforceable Play policy violation.

The policy's 'That's the full list' is false. public/privacy.html:73 enumerates five items then closes 'That's the full list. We do not collect your real name, location, device fingerprint, or any contact list.' Prod holds device_tokens (35 rows: user_id, token, platform — APNs/FCM tokens), web_push_subscriptions (endpoint, subscription jsonb, tz_offset_minutes — a coarse location signal), notifications (11), question_reports (45), club_quiz_results (205), room_answers (1,910), challenge_events. The strings 'notification', 'push' and 'device token' appear 0 times in public/privacy.html. Android FCM push went live yesterday and the policy was not touched.

No Clarity masking hardening anywhere. Zero data-clarity-mask / clarity-unmask attributes in src/ or index.html. The signed-in Settings screen renders the account email as a plain text node (src/App.jsx:6158-6160). Clarity's default masking mode masks form-field text, not rendered text nodes — so unless the project is set to Strict in the Clarity console (unverified; MCP can't read project settings), replays of signed-in web sessions contain the user's email, username and friends list. The policy's claim is only 'session replays with typed text masked', which does not cover rendered text.

No web-accessible deletion route, while Play's listing promises one. The only path the policy names is 'Settings → Account → Delete Account' (public/privacy.html:62), which requires the app installed and a working sign-in. Play requires apps with account creation to offer an off-app request channel too. privacy@balliq.app is offered only 'if you have any questions about this privacy policy', not as a deletion channel — and per the repo's own notes balliq.app mail is inbound-only, so a deletion request could not even be answered.

docs/STORE_LISTINGS.md — the repo's supposed record of what was submitted — is wrong in both directions. Line ~255: 'Device IDs | No | — | — | We don't collect device IDs' (live Play declares Device or other IDs). Line ~253: crash logs 'Yes' (live Play declares nothing). Nobody can audit the store forms from the repo, which is how gap #4 survived.

No app-level PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. `find ios -name '*.xcprivacy'` returns only built Capacitor.framework / Cordova.framework manifests; ios/App/App/ has none. 1.6.0 was approved so this has not bitten yet, but the app target reaches required-reason APIs (UserDefaults via Capacitor Preferences, file timestamps) and ITMS-91053 enforcement only tightens. Latent submission blocker, not a current one.

result.verdict: The first screen a stranger sees is still a playable football question with no login, which is genuinely better than most quiz apps ship — but a month of onboarding work has produced two unverifiable engineering claims, an activation funnel that fires events nobody can read, and prod data showing 38% of new accounts still never play anything.
strengths: Zero-tap, zero-auth first frame, verified live: with the service worker unregistered, 3 balliq-v10 caches deleted and localStorage cleared, https://balliq.app/play rendered the taster question ("Who has scored the most goals in men's international football?") as the literal first screen at 375x812 — screenshotted. No welcome copy, no login wall.

The pre-boot shell is structurally sound engineering, whatever the noisy numbers say: #preboot-onboard is inline static HTML at char 42,073 of a 58.5 KB document, placed FIRST in <body> (char 39,952) ahead of all hidden homepage prose; both Google Fonts links use the media="print"/onload swap with a <noscript> fallback so neither blocks paint; the only render-blocking stylesheet is /assets/index-C_mObk-c.css at 312 bytes. Deep-link deferral is unusually careful and correct: App.jsx:8008-8031 snapshots BOOT_PATH/BOOT_SEARCH at module eval (because a replaceState side-effect in a sibling useState initializer plus StrictMode double-invocation used to silently no-op every deferral), validates club/quiz slugs against the module maps so a dead link can't suppress onboarding for nothing, and deliberately does NOT write biq_onboarded — so a search visitor plays the club quiz first and still gets the taster on their first organic Home visit.

Guest play actually migrates on sign-in: useAuth.jsx:530-570 back-syncs every local-only biq_daily_<ymd> and biq_wordle_<ymd> through upsert_daily_score / upsert_wordle_state, so the "save your progress" prompt at App.jsx:10052 is not lying to the player — the two most-played modes carry over.

Account pressure stays minimal and peak-timed: App.jsx:10052 is the only signup ask a guest gets, gated on isGuest && !nudged && peak with explicit anti-stacking guards against the rate prompt, notification sheet, level-up and challenge settlement. Prod confirms the guest-first order holds — all 124 profiles created in the last 30 days have onboarded_at set (they onboarded before they could sign up).
weaknesses: 38% of accounts since guest-first still never play. Prod SQL: of 179 profiles created on/after 2026-06-23 and older than 24h, 68 have no scores row AND empty daily_scores AND empty wordle_state. Split by cohort the direction is unflattering — pre-guest-first accounts played at 80.0% (16/20), post-guest-first at 62.3% (101/162), last 2 days 58.8% (10/17). Guest daily/Footle play DOES back-sync on sign-in, so this is mostly not a sync artefact for the two big modes (Trail/Mystery/Stadiums/club-quiz guest play does not back-sync, which softens but does not erase it). The previous panel's "structurally gone" is not supported by the database.

The activation instrumentation cannot be read. loopEvent() at App.jsx:1900-1904 fires window.clarity("event", name) — Clarity's data-export API returns only its own auto-detected smart events (last 7d: Other 973, Play 76, SubmitForm 16, SignUp 8, OutboundClick 7, ContinueAsGuest 1); my explicit query for onboard-done-answered / onboard-done-skipped / first-game-started returned []. The instrumentation is also blind on native. loopEvent() is guarded `if (!IS_NATIVE ...)` (App.jsx:1901), and the pre-boot shell's reveal script bails on `if(native)return`. So both of this month's onboarding improvements — the fast first paint and the activation funnel — apply only to web, and skip the App Store / Play funnel that the 10 newly-localised Play listings (743565a, 2026-08-20) are built to feed.

The lab claim doesn't reproduce. Four PSI mobile runs on /play today: perf 0.99 / 0.75 / 0.66 / 0.59, LCP 1,800 / 5,000 / 6,154 / 11,000 ms, FCP 1.2 / 3.3 / 3.8 / 6.1 s. result.verdict: Sentry receives events from WEB ONLY — the shipped iOS 1.6.2 (build 65) and Android bundles contain the Sentry SDK with no DSN and no client, so every captureException in the native app silently drops. Crash-free rate for native is not merely unknown, it is unmeasurable; and CI has reported "success" on 30 consecutive runs while its e2e job failed every single time. The in-app crash *handling* (boot watchdogs, error boundaries) is genuinely good; the crash *visibility* and the release gate are worse than anyone realised.
strengths: Boot path is properly hardened against the documented hang class — three independent bounded timers, not .catch()es: a 5s getSession watchdog (src/useAuth.jsx:157) that enters guest mode on a hang, a 2s profile-wait cap (src/App.jsx:12060), and an 8s native splash failsafe (src/main.jsx) that lifts an unhideable splash regardless. Verified live: cold-terminated and relaunched iOS 1.6.2 on the simulator — splash to a fully rendered Home in under 5s.

ErrorBoundary placement is the result of real incident learning, not boilerplate: it sits ABOVE both lazy roots in src/main.jsx (so a rejected React.lazy import is caught) and AGAIN above AuthProvider in src/GameRoot.jsx:19 (so an auth-init throw isn't a white screen). componentDidCatch calls SplashScreen.hide() first — otherwise the fallback's 'Restart App' button renders under an unhideable native splash.

Stale-chunk self-heal after deploys: src/main.jsx listens for vite:preloadError and unhandledrejection, matches ChunkLoadError shapes, and reloads once behind a sessionStorage guard — web-only, correctly gated off native where chunks are bundled.

Web-side Sentry is configured properly end to end, not just installed. Read live from balliq.app/play: client DSN o4511344022061056.ingest.de.sentry.io, environment=production, release=fdcb109 (matches git HEAD), transport initialised, tracesSampleRate 0.1. Source maps were uploaded (2 _sentryDebugIds in the live bundle) and are NOT publicly served (index-Bnf4vgjN.js.map returns 404) — symbolicated stacks without leaking the question bank.

The web app is empirically stable. Microsoft Clarity, last 7 days: 749 sessions, 1 JavaScript error, 2 rage clicks, 92 dead clicks. That is a real, measured low error rate — not an absence of instrumentation.

scripts/preflight-release.mjs is a well-designed gate: it checks artifacts rather than intent (fresh build + content-hashed filename parity against both native projects), which catches ANY dist/native drift, not just the Trail-anchor near-miss that prompted it.
Backend error rate is low: 8 HTTP 500 and 9 HTTP 400 out of 4,582 edge_logs requests in 24h (0.17%), with zero ERROR/FATAL/PANIC rows in postgres_logs.
weaknesses: CRITICAL — neither native shell reports crashes at all. Native builds are cut locally (`rm -rf dist && npm run build && npx cap sync`), and /Users/alexanderbrynolsen/ball-iq/.env.local contains only VITE_SUPABASE_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and PAGESPEED_API_KEY — no VITE_SENTRY_DSN. Because src/main.jsx wraps the whole init in `if (import.meta.env.VITE_SENTRY_DSN)`, Rollup drops it. The installed iOS 1.6.2 build 65 on the simulator has 0 occurrences of `dsn:`, 0 of `init(`, 0 of `ingest`; the android/ and ios/ asset trees are byte-identical to dist. What survives is the SDK's Scope shim carrying the literal string "No client configured on scope - will not capture exception!" — that is the runtime behaviour of every Sentry call in the native app. The answer to the panel's question is: web only.

Even with the DSN set, @sentry/react structurally cannot see the crashes that have actually hit this app. Ticket #1650 (commit f50dccf, 2026-07-12) was 'Default FirebaseApp is not initialized' hard-crashing every Android device outside the JS bridge — a JS SDK never sees that. package.json has @sentry/react only; there is no @sentry/capacitor, no sentry-android, no sentry-cocoa. So native-layer crashes are invisible by design, not by misconfiguration.

result.verdict: This is worse than "never attempted": Ball IQ is structurally ineligible for the featuring surfaces it would want, and the two dated windows it had this season expired three days ago inside its own TODO. Against Apple's seven published criteria it scores near-zero on four of them — the binary is English-only (`languageCodesISO2A = ['EN']`), it is iPhone-only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1"`, 0 iPad screenshots), it ships zero Apple platform technology (no WidgetKit, no Live Activities, no App Intents, Game Center off), and its product page carries 2 ratings, no App Preview video, and a first screenshot with a rendering artifact that is live on the store right now.
strengths: The UI genuinely clears Apple's criteria 1-2. I drove the booted simulator (1.6.2) and the Home screen is confident, hierarchical, dark-mode-native, with real typographic rhythm and a coherent green/amber accent system. This is not the weak link — an editor looking at pixels would not reject it.

Criterion 4 (uniqueness) is real. Footle, Transfer Trail and Mystery Player are original mechanics, not the generic 4-option quiz that the nine competing 'Football Quiz - Soccer Trivia' clones on the store all ship. The differentiation exists; it is just not being narrated to anyone.

The editorial founder-story hook already exists in-product: Settings > About reads "Built solo in Norway 🇳🇴" and the App Store description says "Hand-curated questions, not AI-generated noise." That is exactly the human/creative angle Apple's nomination form asks for — it is written, just never submitted.

Store metadata hygiene is above indie average: correct dual-genre placement (Games > Puzzle > Trivia > Sports), a disciplined name/subtitle/keyword split with a documented no-shared-word rule, and a checked-in localisations.json as source of truth rather than console typing.

Categories and the calendar were understood. docs/TODO.md:930-939 correctly identifies the ASC Featuring > Nominations path, the 3-week Apple lead, Play promotional content, In-App Event badge types, and the 5.2.1 IP trap from the prior World Cup rejection. The thinking was done.
weaknesses: ZERO nominations have ever been submitted. docs/TODO.md:930-939 is headed "⏰ EXPIRES MON 18 AUG" and both boxes are still unchecked on 21 Aug. UCL MD1 is 8-10 Sep = 18 days out, inside Apple's stated 3-week floor. The one dated, free, no-binary-required distribution lever this season was identified, scoped, and then allowed to lapse.

Criterion 6 (Localization) is a hard zero and the repo is fooling itself about it. store-assets/1.6.1/localisations.json carries 14 locales and play-localisations.json carries 10 — but that is STORE TEXT only. There is no i18n library in package.json, no locale files under src/, no CFBundleLocalizations, and only Base.lproj in the bundle. The live listing confirms it: languageCodesISO2A = ['EN']. A Spanish listing that opens an English app is worse than no listing for an editor.

Criterion 5 (Accessibility) fails on Dynamic Type. src/app.css has 418 `font-size: Npx` declarations and zero rem/em; `text-size-adjust` appears nowhere in src/ or index.html. In a WKWebView that means iOS Dynamic Type has literally no effect. The aria-live and colour-blind work (177 aria-labels, 24 prefers-reduced-motion rules) is good but it is the half Apple's editors do not check first.

Criterion 7 is undermined by a live defect. The first App Store screenshot, downloaded from mzstatic right now, has ghost content bleeding through the frosted tab bar: a flame glyph sits over the "Daily" label so it reads "🔥aily", plus a phantom card outline and a translucent blob over the Home icon. Its md5 is identical to store-assets/1.6.0 and 1.6.1, so this has been the first impression since 19 Aug.

No App Preview video exists on either store. There is not a single .mp4/.mov/.m4v anywhere under store-assets/, store-screenshots/ or screenshots/, and the live Play HTML contains no YouTube embed. Google's featuring guide treats a promo video as table stakes; Apple's criterion 7 names app previews explicitly.

iPad is excluded by build setting, not by choice. TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1" at project.pbxproj:371/392 and ipadScreenshotUrls: 0 on the live listing mean Ball IQ shows as "Designed for iPhone" on every iPad surface. Pass-and-Play for 2-6 people around one screen is the single most iPad-shaped feature in the product and it cannot be featured there.

Criterion 3 (Innovation via platform technology) is zero on iOS. ios/App/App contains exactly two Swift files (AppDelegate.swift, ShareCardPlugin.swift); project.pbxproj has one PBXNativeTarget of type com.apple.product-type.application and no WidgetKit/ActivityKit/app-extension references at all. Android already ships a working daily widget (DailyWidgetProvider.java, widget_daily.xml) — iOS has nothing. isGameCenterEnabled = False despite the app being built on streaks and leaderboards.

2 ratings. userRatingCount = 2 on the live listing. Apple's product-page criterion names "positive ratings and reviews"; a 5.0 from two people reads to an editor as no signal, and Play shows no Editors' Choice or download-tier badge either.

The TODO's Play deadline is wrong in a way that killed a still-live lever. It says Play needs 14 days for Deadline Day (1 Sep) and marks it expired. Google's published guidance is to submit promotional content at least four days before the start date; the longer lead applies to the featuring request. Alex can still publish a Deadline Day card on his own store listing on the biggest single traffic day of the transfer calendar — he has simply forfeited the featuring tick.

There is no pitch artefact. No editorial one-pager, no press kit, no nomination draft anywhere in docs/ — PARTNERSHIP-PITCH.md is a media-backlink play, not a store-editorial one. The 'what would the pitch say' question has no existing answer to critique.

result.verdict: There is no revenue path at all — not a weak one, a nonexistent one: no billing SDK, no entitlement table, no price, no product definition, and zero ad requests firing on prod. The one path in flight (AdSense) would earn roughly $13–26/mo at the site's measured 2,570 pageviews even if approved tomorrow, which does not cover the $25/mo Supabase bill.
strengths: Cost discipline is genuinely good and the 'cost ceiling' worry is unfounded. Supabase org plan is confirmed `pro` ($25/mo) with the database at 22 MB against 8 GB included (0.27%) and 205 lifetime auth users against 100,000 MAU included (0.2%). Supabase spend caps are ON by default on Pro, so the bill is hard-capped at $25 unless deliberately disabled — a 50× season-start spike (~128k pageviews) still lands inside both Vercel Pro's 1 TB and Supabase's 250 GB included egress. The exposure Alex was worried about does not exist.

The dormant ad code is properly built and properly guarded — not half-wired. `src/lib/ads.js` refuses to run in the installed PWA, in Capacitor, or with an empty AD_CLIENT; `scripts/gen-seo-pages.mjs:656` sets `ADS_ACTIVE = false`; and I verified on prod that a club page fires zero requests to pagead2/googlesyndication/fundingchoices and renders zero `ins.adsbygoogle` elements. The earlier call to switch the CMP off after Lighthouse measured its cost was correct — this is dormant with no perf tax, not rotting.

'No ads' is a real differentiator, not just an absence. Every single comparable App Store listing I pulled carries the `ContainsAdvertising` flag — Guess the Soccer Player, Trivela Quiz, Goal! Quiz, Perfect Ten, TikiTaka. Ball IQ's listing says 'No ads — no third-party ad trackers, and your data is never sold.' In a category that is uniformly ad-stuffed, that is a defensible position worth protecting.

The question bank is the one asset at genuinely licensable scale: 6,694 questions in `src/questions.js`, fact-checked, with a build-gated distractor-plausibility audit and an era policy. `docs/PARTNERSHIP-PITCH.md` already documents a Norwegian competitor (fcQuiz, ~27k visits/mo) trading exactly this asset to FotMob for weekly syndication. Nobody has priced it.
weaknesses: Zero monetisation infrastructure exists, verified three independent ways. `package.json` dependencies contain no RevenueCat, no StoreKit wrapper, no Play Billing, no Stripe — the only commerce-adjacent Capacitor plugin is `@capacitor-community/in-app-review`. The prod `public` schema has 17 tables and none is purchases/entitlements/subscriptions. `profiles` has 11 columns and none is an entitlement flag. Shipping any paid tier is a multi-week build from zero, not a config flip.

The stated Pro plan has no price, no spec, and no inventory. `PRODUCT.md:73` is the entire strategy: 'Content is free and stays free. Paid tier, if it happens, is features and cosmetics.' But there is no cosmetics catalogue anywhere in `src/` — no AVATARS constant exists; `avatar_id` is a raw emoji string defaulting to '⚽' (`src/useAuth.jsx:305`) and the custom avatar upload is already built and already free. 'Pro = cosmetics' currently means selling an empty shelf.

AdSense is under water even in the success case. Clarity measures 2,226 sessions / 2,570 pageviews over the last 30 days. At an EEA sports/games RPM of $5–10 that is ~$13–26/mo against a known fixed cost floor of ~$33/mo (Supabase Pro $25 + Apple Developer $99/yr amortised) and likely ~$53/mo if Vercel Pro is in the stack, as `docs/MONITORING_OPTIONS.md:30` implies. The application has been stuck since 5 July — seven weeks — waiting for a channel that cannot pay the hosting bill.

The board is blocking Mediavine on a threshold that no longer exists. `docs/TODO.md:1406` defers the monetisation checkpoint to '~10k sessions/month'. Journey by Mediavine dropped to 1,000 sessions/month on 15 January 2026 at a 70% rev share; Ezoic removed its minimum entirely in 2023; Raptive cut to 25,000 pageviews in October 2025. Ball IQ has cleared the Journey bar for some time and nobody has looked. (Caveat before anyone acts: Journey requires the Grow plugin and non-WordPress eligibility is unconfirmed — verify first.)

The live privacy policy states a falsehood in the present tense, and it contradicts the store listing. `public/privacy.html:57` (verified live on prod) reads 'Our website (balliq.app) shows ads via Google' and line 82 says the site 'also displays ads through Google AdSense' and that EEA users 'will be asked for your consent choices through a Google-certified consent prompt'. No ads serve and no CMP loads — I measured zero such network requests. The same text is duplicated inside the native app at `src/App.jsx:6746`, on a build whose App Store listing declares 'No ads'.

The paid-apps paperwork is unstarted and is on the critical path for every IAP route. Apple's Paid Applications Agreement (bank details, tax forms, a Norwegian entity) and a Google Play merchant account both carry multi-week lead times, and nothing in the repo or the board references them. The Settings screen I walked top-to-bottom in the simulator has no 'Restore Purchases' row — correctly, since nothing is sold, but it is a reminder that the App Store review requirement has never been designed for.

The category's proven monetiser has been given away twice over. Measured live App Store prices: 'Remove Ads' one-time at $1.99 (Perfect Ten, TikiTaka) and $2.99 (Guess the Soccer Player, Trivela, Goal! Quiz); MatchCall Pro is $2.99 one-time for remove-ads plus push. Ball IQ has no ads to remove, and the second-most-common lever — paid hints — is a free toggle in Settings ('Show Hints', screenshotted). The only subscription anywhere in the comparable set is Sporcle Plus at $3.99/mo or $29.99/yr, and Sporcle is a 15-year-old platform. The planned subscription has no precedent in this category.

The arithmetic says monetisation is currently impossible, and nobody has written that down. 90 distinct players in the last 30 days; only 27 played on 5+ days, 13 on 10+, and 3 on 20+. A $2.99 one-time unlock at a generous 2% conversion of MAU is ~2 sales/mo ≈ $5 net after the 15% Small Business Program rate — a fifth of the Supabase bill. Break-even on infra alone needs ~13 buyers/mo, i.e. ~650 monetisable MAU at 2%, against 90 today. 'Pro (2.0)' is an undated aspiration attached to no trigger.

result.verdict: The desktop shell is further along than the roadmap claims — Home, Daily, Profile, Online and the quiz screen all have real ≥1024px layouts, and desktop performance is a 99 — but the journey breaks at exactly the money points: the onboarding taster and the sign-up wall are unstyled mobile columns floating in black, the browser Back button silently exits the app mid-game, and A/B/C/D badges promise a keyboard that was never wired. Tablet is not "half-done", it is a genuine zero: there is not one CSS rule between 361px and 1023px, so an iPad in portrait gets a 420px column under a 785px navigation bar.
strengths: The desktop app shell is MORE complete than the roadmap memory says. Home, Daily, Profile and Online all render a proper three-zone desktop layout (left rail + main column + right stats sidebar) at 1440 and 1920. The note that only Home was rebuilt is stale — I screenshotted all four.

Desktop performance is excellent and has never been credited: PageSpeed desktop scores 99 for /play (LCP 0.8s, CLS 0.041, TBT 0ms) and 98 for /quiz/barcelona/ (LCP 0.4s). This is a completely different world from the 4,014ms mobile cold LCP in the notes.

The SEO/marketing layer is genuinely desktop-native and is the best-designed surface in the product. /quiz/barcelona/ at 1440 has a real two-column hero, a top nav with dropdowns, and a playable inline taster on the right — it does not read as a phone page at all.
The quiz screen adapts properly at desktop: a 2x2 answer grid with letter badges rather than a stacked mobile list, and the explanation/Next state holds together at 1440.
Footle has full physical-keyboard support — I dispatched real keydowns and watched tiles fill (HAAL__). It ignores modifier combos so cmd-R still works. src/App.jsx:7586-7593.

Focus-visible is handled globally, not piecemeal: one rule at src/app.css:156 covers button/a/.opt/.cta/.play-card/.mode-item/.tab-item/.icon-btn/input/[role=button]. Keyboard users get a visible 2px accent ring everywhere.

Wide-screen behaviour at 1920 is deliberate and holds — .app is capped at 2600px and left-anchored to the rail (src/app.css:2726-2744), with a documented rationale. No abandoned dead zone on Home at 1920.

The installed-PWA killswitch is real: a @media(display-mode:standalone) block resets the desktop reflow so an installed PWA stays byte-identical to mobile (src/app.css:2757+). That is a trap most solo projects fall into.
weaknesses: THE TABLET BAND IS ENTIRELY UNHANDLED. Full breakpoint census of src/app.css: 8x (min-width:1024px), 1x (min-width:1280px), 1x (max-width:1023px), 1x (max-width:360px). Zero rules target 361-1023px. The responsive system is binary — phone or desktop — with nothing in between.

Confirmed on a real iPad, not just emulation: iPad Air 11-inch simulator, Safari, portrait. Content column is ~420pt centred, with ~200pt of dead black down each side, while the bottom tab bar spans the full width — the 'Home' pill sits ~180pt to the LEFT of the content it belongs to, 'Profile' hangs off the right edge. Measured at 820px viewport: .app = 420px at x=193; .tab-bar = 785px at x=10. The nav is 1.87x wider than the content.

The two highest-leverage desktop screens are the two that were never touched. At 1440x900 the first-run onboarding taster is a ~340px column stranded in a black void, and the sign-up wall ('Save your progress' / Continue with Apple/Google/email) is a mobile sheet with a ~230px empty gap between the copy and the buttons. These are the first screen a desktop visitor sees and the conversion gate — both look unfinished.

BROWSER BACK IS UNWIRED. Navigating Home -> Profile -> Footle leaves location.pathname at '/play' and history.length at 1. history.pushState is used ONLY for modals (src/useModalA11y.js:133) — there is no screen-level routing anywhere in src/. On desktop, Back is a reflex: pressing it mid-Footle or mid-quiz drops the user out of the app entirely and loses the run. No screen is bookmarkable or shareable.

The A/B/C/D badges are a promise the app does not keep. Options render A (src/App.jsx:2071 and :3500) — the universal signal for keyboard shortcuts on every quiz competitor — but no key binding exists. I dispatched 'a' and '1' on a live question: nothing happened. Only Footle has a global keydown listener.

No focus management between question states. After answering, document.activeElement stays on the answered .opt button; pressing Enter does nothing (verified — still on the explanation). A desktop player must mouse to 'Next' seven times per Daily 7.

Settings is unrefreshed at desktop: a ~700px left-anchored single column with roughly 60% of a 1920 viewport empty to its right. Results is half-refreshed — a ~570px column centred in the leftover space rather than aligned to the app's own grid.

The hero CTA on the top desktop landing pages is two dead ends. On /quiz/barcelona/ the only hero links are App Store and Google Play (verified via DOM). Desktop was 124 of 355 Clarity sessions (35%) over 3 days, and PC sessions land on /quiz/barcelona (10), /quiz/liverpool (9), /quiz/arsenal (8). The subline says 'plays in your browser' but there is no button for it.

There is no iPad app and the iPad config is dead code. TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1" at ios/App/App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:371 and :392 — iPhone only. Info.plist still carries UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad = Portrait, config that can never fire. Consequence: Ball IQ is not offered as an iPad app in the iPad App Store's default results.

Android has no orientation lock and no screenSizes declaration (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) — resizeableActivity defaults true on modern targetSdk. So Android tablets, foldables and Chromebooks run the app full-screen at exactly the 820-1023px width that has no CSS, i.e. the broken tab-bar layout above.

Rotating a tablet swaps the entire navigation model. At 1180x820 (iPad landscape) you get the desktop left rail and no bottom tab bar; rotate to 820x1180 and the rail vanishes and a full-width bottom tab bar appears. Same device, two different apps.

The desktop rail's active item carries no aria-current or aria-selected — all five .bn-item buttons return null for both. (I checked the accessible names too: they come from visible text and are fine, so this is the only real gap.)

The brief's premise that most organic traffic is desktop is overstated. Measured over 2026-08-19 to 08-21: Mobile 222, PC 124, Tablet 9 sessions. Desktop is 35% of sessions, not a majority — still a third of the audience playing a product with a broken back button, but worth sizing correctly before investing.

result.movement: It moved WITHIN the band, not across it, so the grade stays 7. Two of the previous panel's four quick wins genuinely landed and I verified both live on prod: the colour-blind Footle palette works (measured rgb(245,121,58) on tiles AND keyboard with html.biq-cb active) and the guess narration fires correctly (read back: "Guess 1 of 6: M not in name, O correct spot, D not in name, R correct spot, I not in name, C not in name."). A third gain nobody asked for also landed: a71cade gave every Footle key its half of the dead 2px/6px gaps as touch area (38.4x48 to 40.4x54) and fixed ENTER sitting below the fold on iPhone SE. That is real motor-accessibility work. The grade does not rise, for three reasons. (1) The colour-blind mode ships with two holes I measured: the Home Footle hero grid (.fh-tile-green/.fh-tile-yellow, ZERO biq-cb overrides in app.css) still renders rgb(88,204,2)/rgb(255,193,7) with the toggle ON, and that is the most-seen Footle surface in the app; and the share PNG hard-codes the same green/amber at App.jsx:3931 while only the emoji fallback reads CB_MODE(). (2) The highest-traffic surface is untouched: I answered a question live on balliq.app/quiz/liverpool/ and grading is still class 'bq-o ok'/'bq-o no' with the chips reading "A"/"D", no glyph, on a page with 0 aria-live regions. The f8fa7ac message says the SEO taster "already had them" -- true of the .to taster (gen-seo-pages.mjs:846), NOT of the .bq-o club quiz (gen-seo-pages.mjs:1172) that fires clubq-play. The glyph fix went to the wrong taster. (3) A fresh negative: Name the Stadium shipped 2026-08-20, the day AFTER the panel, with 5 aria attributes in the whole file; Trail has 4, Mystery 2. The standard is not being carried into new code, so the problem surface grows about as fast as it is fixed. Also note none of this is live to a single store user yet: 1.6.0/vc19 are the shipped builds and predate f8fa7ac. Web only.
result.verdict: The single worst failure the last panel named -- Footle being colour-only for ~1-in-12 male fans -- is genuinely fixed and I watched it work, and the Footle keyboard got a real touch-target win on top. But the fix has two measured holes, the club pages that carry ~half of all impressions still grade answers by tint with zero screen-reader feedback, and three modes shipped since with almost no ARIA at all. Strong foundations, uneven application.
strengths: Colour-blind mode is real and works. Verified live on https://balliq.app/footle with html.biq-cb active: tiles rgb(245,121,58) (#F5793A) and keyboard keys the same; screenshotted the board and it is unmistakably orange. Under Vienot deuteranopia the CB pair separates by hue (#AAAA2D olive vs #B1B1FA lavender) where the default pair does not (#B4B41C vs #D6D600; protanopia luminance ratio 1.06, i.e. identical).

Footle guess narration is live and correct. Read the aria-live region on prod after a submit: "Guess 1 of 6: M not in name, O correct spot, D not in name, R correct spot, I not in name, C not in name." Announces the latest guess only, so it does not bury new information under five rows of old.

Touch targets improved measurably where they could. Footle key measured 35.7x48 painted at 375pt, with a ::after inset:-3px -1px slop that tiles the dead gaps exactly (app.css:1739), taking the effective target to ~37.7x54. Width is arithmetically capped by ten full-bleed keys; the gaps were the only thing left and they were taken.

The main quiz engine's reveal is genuinely non-colour-dependent, and I confirmed it on the iOS Simulator: filled green chip with a checkmark, red chip with a cross, plus a separate "x Incorrect" text verdict below the options. A colour-blind or low-vision player gets three redundant channels.

Automated accessibility is clean on both surfaces. Lighthouse accessibility scored 1.00 (100) on https://balliq.app/play and on https://balliq.app/quiz/liverpool/, headless mobile, run today. Zero failing audits on either.
Contrast holds up everywhere I measured, including the newer surfaces: CB orange tile text 7.24:1, CB blue tile 10.28:1, eliminated-key text (white 60% over #3A3F55) 4.92:1. All clear AA.
Localised SEO pages are properly internationalised at the page level: /es/quiz/river-plate/ serves lang="es", hreflang es / en / x-default, a skip-to-content link, and fully Spanish copy.
weaknesses: The colour-blind toggle does not cover the Home Footle hero. Measured with html.biq-cb present: .fh-tile-green computes rgb(88, 204, 2) and .fh-tile-yellow rgb(255, 193, 7). app.css has zero `biq-cb .fh-tile` rules. This is the grid a player sees on every single Home visit, and it renders in exactly the palette they just asked the app to stop using.

The Footle share PNG ignores the toggle. App.jsx:3931 hard-codes colorMap = { green: "#58CC02", yellow: "#FFC107" }. CB_MODE() is referenced only at App.jsx:5127 and 7657 (the two emoji-grid builders). On native, shareCard renders the PNG and the emoji string is only the textFallback, so the primary share path posts a green/amber image that contradicts what the player saw and is unreadable to the friend who shares their condition.

The club-page quiz -- the widget on the pages carrying ~47-51% of impressions -- still fails WCAG 1.4.1 and 4.1.3. Answered a question live on /quiz/liverpool/ today: options became class 'bq-o no' and 'bq-o ok' with chips still reading "A" and "D", no check/cross written. Page has 0 aria-live/role=status/role=alert elements out of 168 .bq-o buttons. Under deuteranopia the two chip backgrounds simulate to #B4B41C vs #9D9D3A (luminance ratio 1.30) -- effectively the same olive.

Hot Streak still reveals correct/wrong by colour alone. App.jsx:2071 renders {['A','B','C','D'][i]} on the graded state, while the main engine one component over swaps in a check or cross (App.jsx:2744). Quick win #3 from the last panel was not done.

No text scaling anywhere. 299 px font-size declarations in app.css, 0 rem, no -webkit-text-size-adjust, no font: -apple-system-body. In a Capacitor WKWebView that means iOS Larger Text and Android font-size settings do nothing at all to Ball IQ. Pinch-zoom survives (no maximum-scale) but that is not a substitute. Zero prefers-contrast support too.

New modes are shipping without the standard. Name the Stadium landed 2026-08-20 -- the day after the last panel -- with 5 aria attributes total (one aria-live, on a progress counter). Transfer Trail has 4 and no live region despite revealing clubs one at a time. Mystery Player has 2 and no live region; its rank number is at least a non-colour cue, but a screen-reader player submits a guess and hears nothing.

The Footle legend is still aria-hidden="true" (verified in the live DOM), so the only place the colour convention is stated in words is invisible to screen readers -- the exact users who most need the convention described rather than shown.

The header settings button, the door to the accessibility toggle itself, is 40x40. .hdr-ic (app.css:1505) explicitly overrides .icon-btn's 44px down to 40px. Two other Home controls measured 20-20.5px tall: "Set your name" (98.6x20) and the daily-zone status link (65.4x20.5), both under WCAG 2.2's 24px minimum as well as Apple's 44.

The UI is 100% English -- zero i18n hits across src -- while /es/quiz/river-plate/ is fully Spanish and its CTA points at https://balliq.app/play?club=river-plate. A Spanish reader converts from a Spanish page straight into an English-only product. I will correct the last panel here though: measured Clarity traffic for 19-21 Aug puts UK+US at 160 sessions against Italy+Spain+Greece+Egypt at 30, roughly 11% of the top-10 mix. This is a real gap but it is not the biggest one, and calling UI localisation the top inclusivity move was over-weighted.

Minor but visible in my screenshot: eliminated Footle keys render rgb(58,63,85) -- LIGHTER and more prominent than untried keys at rgb(28,31,40). Wordle darkens eliminated letters. The letters you should ignore are the ones that pop, which is backwards for anyone scanning the keyboard with low vision. Also, in CB mode the ENTER key stays #58CC02, leaving green as the only unexplained colour on the board.

five_star_moves.title: Move the type ramp to rem and turn on OS text scaling
five_star_moves.why: 299 px font-sizes and 0 rem in app.css means iOS Larger Text and Android font-size do literally nothing inside the app. This is the single largest untouched barrier, it affects far more people than colour-blindness, it is mechanical work a codemod can do in an afternoon, and it is the kind of thing the older 1990s-era-questions demographic notices immediately.

five_star_moves.title: Gate the a11y invariant in the build, don't fix it per-commit
five_star_moves.why: Stadiums shipped a day after the last panel with 5 aria attributes; the colour-blind mode shipped missing two surfaces; the taster glyph fix went to the wrong taster. Three independent misses in one week is a process signal, not a diligence signal. Add a check to the existing npm run build gate that fails when a component styles a correct/wrong state without a text/glyph sibling, or renders a game result with no live region -- the same way the distractor-plausibility audit already gates content.

result.verdict: The security posture is markedly better than the brief assumed — anon holds literally zero table grants in prod, and the grants are column-level least-privilege — but the observability posture is near zero, and that gap has already cost something real: four live accounts hold 485k–595k XP with zero games played, written on 2026-08-08, sitting undetected in the leaderboard for 13 days. Capacity and bill are non-issues at 10x; what would actually hurt is that nobody would know.
strengths: anon role has ZERO table access in production — probed live with the real publishable key from the shipped bundle, all 10 tables return 42501 permission denied. The repo memory's 'anon-full-DML defaults' worry is closed, verified by two routes (information_schema.role_table_grants returned no anon rows at all, and the live REST probe).

Grants are column-level least-privilege, not just table-level. `authenticated` has UPDATE on profiles for avatar_id, avatar_url, correct_answers, games_played, onboarded_at, stats, username — and deliberately NOT total_score or xp, forcing those through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs. I nearly filed a false 'username change is broken' bug off the table-level grant; the column grants are the reason it works. This is more careful than most funded teams manage.

All three anon-callable RPCs already carry hand-written input validation plus silent hourly throttles — log_club_quiz caps at 3,000/hr global and 300/hr per club, record_challenge_event at 500/hr, report_question at 200/hr global, 20/hr per question, plus one-report-per-user dedup. This is real rate limiting at the only unauthenticated write surface, written before anyone asked for it.
Migrated off the legacy anon JWT to the new revocable `sb_publishable_` key format — the shipped bundle carries sb_publishable_FluGERu..., which can be rotated without a client release.

Actual capacity is comfortable and measured, not assumed: 22 MB database, peak 1,315 API requests/hour (2026-08-20 19:00 UTC), zero replication lag, both pg_cron jobs at 100% success over 7 days (168 and 162 runs, zero failures). 10x season-start traffic is ~3.6 requests/second — the current instance does not notice it.

Signup surface is narrower than it could be: anonymous_users is false in prod (the guest-entry toggle really is still off), and profiles/scores/user_game_state RLS policies are all correctly scoped to auth.uid().
weaknesses: LIVE DATA-INTEGRITY INCIDENT, 13 days old, nobody noticed. Four profiles hold 595,620 / 556,875 / 495,550 / 485,485 XP with games_played=0, correct_answers=0 and zero rows in `scores`. All four signed up on 2026-08-08 (4 of that day's 9 signups); no other day in the database has a single profile above 100k XP. These are real users — hotmail.com, icloud.com, proton.me, privaterelay.appleid.com — not test accounts. Whether it was a client bug or someone with curl, the root cause is the same and it is still open.

increment_xp and increment_score accept an unbounded integer delta. Both check `user_id is distinct from auth.uid()` and stop there — no cap, no plausibility check, no CHECK constraint on profiles.xp, no trigger. Any signed-in user can POST one RPC call and top the all-time leaderboard. `scores` is the same story: INSERT policy checks only auth.uid()=user_id, and the table has zero CHECK constraints and zero triggers (current max score is 18, so a submitted 999999 would be conspicuous but accepted).

There is no alerting. None. Sentry is genuinely live (DSN o4511344022061056.ingest.de.sentry.io present in the deployed bundle), but docs/SENTRY_RULES.md line 9 reads 'Last verified: 2026-05-07 (initial setup)' and PRODUCTION_RUNBOOK.md lines 379-386 lists 'confirm a test event reaches Alex's phone' as a BEFORE-LAUNCH task — it is now 3.5 months post-launch and still unverified. grep for 'alert', 'uptime', 'on-call' across the 196 KB docs/TODO.md returns zero hits. It is not late; it is not on the list.

No uptime or synthetic check exists. .github/workflows/ contains exactly two files: ci.yml (push/pull_request only) and spike-nightly.yml (cron 09:00 UTC but blocked on a tier upgrade per its own comment at line 38). result.competitive_edge:
The defensible thing is the EXPLAINED question bank at club depth — and the club pages are where it is measurably converting, which is the part nobody on the panel connected.

The asset: 6,694 questions, 5,626 of them (84.0%) carrying a written explanation, across 86 club packs, with frozen daily schedules and difficulty labels that real player data validates almost perfectly (7 days of club_quiz_results: easy 89.7% correct, medium 69.2%, hard 50.3% — a textbook ladder). The direct competitive field advertises 500 to 1,000+ questions and NOT ONE of them ships per-question explanations. Ball IQ is 6.7x the volume with a story attached to five answers in six. That is not a feature a well-funded rival copies in a sprint; it is thousands of hours of hand-written football prose, and it is the single reason /play holds 92-94% scroll depth and ~103s active time.

The thing that changes the picture: club_quiz_results shows 208 plays in the last 7 days against 210 in the last 30. Essentially all recorded club-page quiz play happened this week — set against 324 total scores rows in the same 7 days, the club-page taster is now roughly 39% of everything played in the product. No panel member surfaced this. Combined with 420 club-page Clarity sessions a week versus 10 on /lists, this says the moat is already converting on one specific surface, and that surface is the one with the layout shift (field CLS 0.11-0.20), the colour-only grading with no glyph and no aria-live, 31% scroll depth, and an uninstrumented return-streak hook.

So the way to press it, in order: (1) make the club-page taster work properly for everyone — glyph, aria-live, no layout shift — because it is already the busiest game in the product and it is currently the least-finished one; (2) keep it FRESH, because 'they already have this week's transfer' is the one thing a 1,000-question static competitor can never say and it is worth more in the first weeks of a season than at any other time; (3) deepen the 17 thin packs so the surface does not run dry after two visits; (4) instrument it, so the next panel argues about measurements rather than about which surface matters.

What is NOT the edge, despite the effort spent on it: cloned daily formats (Mystery Player, the Who-Are-Ya analogue, has 6 plays from 4 players all-time against a 5M-visit incumbent that owns the format), and store listing craft. Ball IQ wins on club depth and explanations. It should stop competing where it structurally cannot.
